summary: DNS search-suffix truncation prevents artifact resolution for on-prem serving nodes
description:
Issue summary: On Acme Health's Private deployment (VPC + VPCE) some on-prem serving nodes intermittently fail to pull model shards and presigned S3 artifacts. Failure mode is DNS resolution returning NXDOMAIN for hostnames that should be resolvable via the customer's split-horizon DNS (search-suffix based discovery).

Impact: Several serving nodes fail to initialize, causing reduced capacity for customers' private pool. Affects model start-up and shard fetches; customer reports ~8% request retries and visible latency spikes on rolling restarts.

Environment: Private deployment behind VPCE in us-east-1. Customer uses internal DNS forwarder that advertises a search list (e.g., svc.acme.internal). Nodes run systemd-resolved with default search behavior. Control plane and artifact fetches traverse VPCE egress through a corporate DNS forwarder/proxy.

Steps to reproduce:
1) On a serving node in the customer's private deployment, run: dig +short model-artifact.s3-presigned
2) Compare resolution with and without the configured search suffix (e.g., model-artifact.s3-presigned.svc.acme.internal).
3) Trigger a model pull via control-plane (redeploy) and observe fetch failures in serving-node logs.

Observed logs/snippets:
- serving-node: "artifact fetch failed: lookup model-artifact.s3-presigned: no such host"
- systemd-resolved: "search domain discarded: total name length > limit" (intermittent)
- tcpdump on node: client sends DNS query for name with search suffix; response is NXDOMAIN when query goes to the customer's forwarder via UDP; when we force TCP query to the same forwarder, server returns the correct A record.

Initial hypothesis: The customer's DNS forwarder (or an intermediary DNS proxy) appears to be truncating or returning NXDOMAIN for long FQDNs produced by the node's search-suffix expansion. UDP responses are truncated/incorrect and TCP fallback is required, but TCP DNS (port 53) is intermittently blocked by the corporate egress appliance leading to resolution failures. systemd-resolved's local search list can produce expanded names longer than 63 octets which some forwarders mishandle, producing NXDOMAIN instead of forwarding correctly.

Notes: This is not an S3 signature or presigned URL validity problem; requests reach S3 when DNS is resolved. The problem is deterministic when search-suffix expansion is used and intermittent when clients resolve strictly-qualified hostnames.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Maya Chen: Ticket created after customer outage alert. They noticed several serving nodes in their private pool never completed startup due to repeated artifact fetch failures.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Asked customer for tcpdump and systemd-resolved logs; requested output of 'resolvectl status' and 'cat /etc/resolv.conf' on an affected node.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (Acme Health - S. Patel): Uploaded packet captures and noted that their corporate egress appliance filters TCP/53 intermittently during business hours; UDP is allowed but upstream forwarder occasionally truncates EDNS0 responses.

2026-03-11 08:45 - SRE (R. Alvarez): Reproduced NXDOMAIN when adding long search-suffix in lab using the customer's forwarder config. Observed correct RRs over TCP. Blocked TCP/53 by the egress appliance reproduces the failure pattern.

2026-03-12 16:05 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Suggested and validated a short-term workaround with customer: set REDWOOD_ARTIFACT_HOST_OVERRIDE to fully-qualified S3 hostnames (avoids search expansion), and added a VPCE private DNS entry for the presigned host in customer's Resolver endpoints.

2026-03-12 18:20 - Customer (S. Patel): Confirmed that nodes recovered after applying host override; rolling restart now shows successful shard downloads. Customer will contact network/security team to allow DNS over TCP to their forwarder or increase UDP EDNS0 buffer support.
investigation_notes: Checked serving-node agent logs (artifact_fetcher). Error consistently 'no such host' concurrent with NXDOMAIN from forwarder over UDP.
Replayed queries from lab replicating customer's resolver chain: UDP path returned TC flag or NXDOMAIN for names > ~140 chars; TCP returned successful answers.

Validated systemd-resolved search expansion can generate FQDNs that exceed 63-character label limits, but total length within 255. Forwarder incorrectly treats long labels as invalid and responds NXDOMAIN instead of REFERRAL/TCP fallback.
Packet captures show corporate egress appliance sometimes drops TCP 53 sessions; pattern correlates with business-hour maintenance windows reported by customer firewall team.

Control-plane logs show repeated retry attempts; we had not previously forced fully-qualified hostnames for artifact resolution in private deployments — relying on client resolver behavior has this risk.
SRE reproduced issue in isolated lab by blocking TCP/53 and using a forwarder that returns truncated EDNS0 responses.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (short-term): Instructed customer to set REDWOOD_ARTIFACT_HOST_OVERRIDE on affected nodes to the canonical presigned S3 host (fully-qualified), bypassing search-suffix expansion. Confirmed artifact pulls succeed after change.
Workaround (alternative): Added alias/host entry in customer's VPCE private DNS zone pointing presigned host -> S3 endpoint; validated model shard downloads.

Engineering mitigation (internal): Opened INT-99827 to add stronger client-side fallback: always attempt resolution of the fully-qualified host (append trailing dot) for artifact fetches before relying on search-suffix expansion. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/2147 created and linked.

Customer action required: Allow DNS over TCP (port 53) to the internal forwarder or upgrade forwarder to honour EDNS0 and avoid truncation for legitimate long queries. Recommended security change request to allow TCP/53 in egress policy for resolver IPs.

Follow-up: Add automated detection to serving-node startup to log and surface 'search-suffix expansion NXDOMAIN' pattern and provide recommended fix hints in Console. Filed INT-99890 for the Console UX change.
Status: Customer confirmed recovery after workaround. Marking as In Progress until client-side fallback PR is merged and customer implements a permanent DNS fix.
